questions.text:
Let $a(x, y)$, $b(x, y)$, and $c(x, y)$ be three statements with variables $x$ and $y$ chosen from some universe. Consider the following statement:


$$(\exists x)(\forall y)[(a(x, y) \wedge b(x, y)) \wedge \neg c(x, y)]$$


Which one of the following is its equivalent?
questions.optA: $(\forall x)(\exists y)[(a(x, y) \vee b(x, y)) \rightarrow c(x, y)]$
questions.optB: $(\exists x)(\forall y)[(a(x, y) \vee b(x, y)) \wedge \neg c(x, y)]$
questions.optC: $\neg(\forall x)(\exists y)[(a(x, y) \wedge b(x, y)) \rightarrow c(x, y)]$
questions.optD: $\neg(\forall x)(\exists y)[(a(x, y) \vee b(x, y)) \rightarrow c(x, y)]$
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: Negating C moves the quantifiers to exists x, for all y and negates the implication. Since not((a AND b) implies c) equals a AND b AND not c, C equals the stem.

questions.text:
Let $R_1$ be a relation from $A = \{1, 3, 5, 7\}$ to $B = \{2, 4, 6, 8\}$ and $R_2$ be another relation from $B$ to $C = \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ as defined below: 
(i) An element $x$ in $A$ is related to an element $y$ in $B$ (under $R_1$) if $x + y$ is divisible by 3. 
(ii) An element $x$ in $B$ is related to an element $y$ in $C$ (under $R_2$) if $x + y$ is even but not divisible by 3. 

Which is the composite relation $R_1R_2$ from $A$ to $C$?
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: R1 sends 1 and 7 to 2,8; 3 to 6; and 5 to 4. R2 sends 2 and 8 to 2; 6 to 2,4; and 4 to 4. Composition is {(1,2),(3,2),(3,4),(5,4),(7,2)}.

$$\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\1&3&4\\2&2&3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}6\\8\\12\end{bmatrix}$$
